about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2019 only.

rows.table: Town and school employee gross wages, calendar 2019
rows.detail: But the WAGE AMOUNTS are almost entirely absent: 39 of roughly 570 appear on p199 and one on p197; pages 198 and 200-203 carry no amounts at all.

rows.table: General fund expenditures pie chart (printed twice)
rows.detail: Percentages do not sum to 100 because the Education slice's label did not OCR.

PAGES 29 AND 31 CARRY THE SAME PIE CHART. Both are headed 'GENERAL FUND EXPENDITURES FY 2019' with identical percentages, but the contents page says p29 (folio 27) should be the General Funds Revenue Chart. The FY2019 report does not contain a general fund revenue chart at all. The previous inventory raised this as unresolvable from the broken text; the corrected text settles it -- the same image was printed twice.

The FY2020 capital plan is printed twice (p107 and p160) and the two printings ARE identical, contrary to what the broken text suggested. The town meeting printing is the more complete of the two: it supplies a Category column and the project name 'Master Plan' that the Capital Planning Committee's own printing lost.

The employee gross wages table is the one financial table the correction did NOT recover. Names now read perfectly in alphabetical order across all seven pages, but only 40 of roughly 570 wage figures survive, all but one of them on a single page. The rotation was never the problem there.

The Fire Department's own call breakdown does not add up: 420 + 949 + 554 + 26 = 1,949 against a stated total of 1,885. The 554 is separately confirmed on the same page as the Fire Prevention Division's inspection count, which suggests inspections are inside one figure and outside the other.

The FY2020 omnibus budget prints Central Purchasing at $603,030.00 on its line and $60,303.00 on its own subtotal row -- a factor of ten apart in a voted budget. The group subtotals only reconcile to the $38,058,164.30 Omnibus total with the smaller figure.

Out-of-district special education placement COUNTS -- the quantity the budget documents never publish -- are stated in plain prose on p119: 12 students outside the district (14 the year before), of which 4 collaborative, 5 day and 3 residential, plus 6 in the ACE programme and 138 students on 504 plans. It is in the Director of Special Services' narrative, not in any table.

The Cemetery Commission publishes every 2019 interment by name and age, with war service annotated, two pages before the Town Clerk explains that names have been removed from the vital records section for the safety and security of residents.

The Public Access Cable Committee publishes a complete profit-and-loss for its own fund -- opening balance, revenue, nine expense lines, and a separately held Comcast capital fund -- and every figure ties to the special revenue funds schedule on p41. No other single department in the report gives anything like it.

rows.table: General fund expenditures pie chart (printed twice)
rows.detail: The table of contents says p29 (folio 27) should be the 'General Funds Revenue Chart'.
The report contradicts itself on which year this is; do not quote a year from this table without checking the PDF.
AREA is printed twice and inconsistently: the panel says 26.63 square miles, the paragraph below says approximately 26.4.

Two pages OCR'd MIRRORED rather than merely rotated -- p116 (school enrollment) and p195 (part of the election results), plus p52 of the debt schedule. Their rows and columns are intact but reversed, which makes them recoverable with care rather than lost.
Some names are still OCR-damaged.

rows.table: FY2020 capital plan (as voted, Annual Town Meeting Article 6)
rows.detail: With the corrected text both printings carry the SAME fourteen projects in the same order; the apparent difference was an OCR artefact.
Some line numbers and a few account names did not OCR.

rows.table: Annual Town Election results by precinct, 18 May 2019
rows.detail: Scattered precinct cells did not OCR, but every contest's TOTAL row survives and the totals reconcile against ballots cast x seats.

rows.table: Town and school employee gross wages, calendar 2019
rows.detail: This is not a row-order problem the rotation fix could touch, so the figures are either faint in the print or dropped by the OCR engine, and the PDF has to be re-read to get them.

rows.table: Combined balance sheet, all fund types, 30 June 2019
rows.detail: Dollar signs are frequently OCR'd as '5' at the start of a figure ('51,286,217.55' = $1,286,217.55).
IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the rendering is hard-clipped at 188 characters.
The first two column pairs survive complete; the THIRD column's labels survive but every one of its AMOUNTS is cut off.

rows.table: Assessor's account for exemptions and abatements
rows.detail: One value has an OCR space: '120, 469.33'.

rows.table: Trust and stabilization funds held by other banks
rows.detail: ENDING VALUE column clipped by the 188-character limit.

rows.table: FY2019 collection of taxes -- receivables summary
rows.detail: The prior inventory recorded that the ADJUSTMENTS column is ALSO physically clipped by the page edge in the printed report; that remains plausible and is not settled by this text.
Only six diseases OCR: Anaplasmosis 2, Arborvirus 1, Campylobacteriosis 2, Cyclosporiasis 1, Hepatitis C 3, Influenza 48.
Those sum to 1,949, which does NOT equal the stated 1,885 -- a discrepancy of 64 that is in the printed report, not in the OCR.
